name: libfdisk script parser (sfdisk dump format reader)
description:
fdisk_script_read_file() parses a text "sfdisk script" (the dump format produced by sfdisk/fdisk -d) line-by-line from an untrusted FILE stream into an in-memory struct fdisk_script, which contains a header list and a fdisk_table of fdisk_partition objects. Because it directly tokenizes attacker-controlled text (header lines like "label: dos", name=value partition lines, and comma-separated legacy lines), and later fdisk_apply_script()/fdisk_apply_table() feed the parsed numeric offsets/sizes/types/UUIDs into the real partition-table engine, this is a classic text-parser attack surface for a C project (buffer handling, integer parsing with strtoX, string quoting/escaping, and downstream use of parsed values to build on-disk structures).
- fdisk_script_read_file: target/entry, reads the whole FILE line by line via fdisk_script_read_line() and dispatches each non-blank/non-comment line to fdisk_script_read_buffer().
- fdisk_new_script: lifecycle entry needed to obtain the struct fdisk_script * the target writes into (also usable without a fdisk_context for a context-free fuzzing path).
- fdisk_new_script_from_file: variant/source that itself calls fdisk_script_read_file() on a path given as a string instead of a FILE*, exercising the identical core logic through the filename API.
- fdisk_script_read_line: lower-level variant of the per-line reader (also public) letting the harness feed single lines or use a custom fgets-like callback (fdisk_script_set_fgets) to control line boundaries.
- fdisk_script_write_file: inverse/consumer operation (dump-format or JSON serializer) that round-trips the parsed table/headers back to text, exercising the data structures the parser filled in.
- fdisk_apply_script: consumer that takes the fully parsed script and applies its headers (fdisk_apply_script_headers, creates a label) and its partition table (fdisk_apply_table) to a fdisk_context, running much more code on the parsed/validated values (types, uuids, start/size) and is the real downstream use of the parser's output in sfdisk.
- fdisk_script_set_header / fdisk_script_get_table: configuration/accessor functions used alongside parsing to inspect or pre-seed state that the core reads (dp->headers, dp->table).
Input space selected by the fuzz data: which of the three per-line grammars is taken (is_header_line() -> "name: value" header line vs. a line containing '=' -> name=value partition fields vs. plain comma/space separated legacy "start,size,type,bootable" line); for header lines, the header name (one of "label","unit","label-id","device","grain","first-lba","last-lba","table-length","sector-size", each with its own validation, e.g. sector-size must be a multiple of 512, unit must be "sectors"); for name=value lines, which partition fields appear (start=, size=, bootable, attrs=, uuid=, name=, type=/Id=) including quoted ("...") and hex-escaped strings for name=, and the leading "<device>:" / "<device> : " partno prefix parsed by partno_from_devname(); for the legacy comma format, the ordered positional fields (start,size,type,bootable,...); plus line-length/EOF edge cases (missing trailing newline, comments '#', blank lines, CRLF) handled directly in fdisk_script_read_line()/fdisk_script_read_file().
